sections.h2: Which Bellefontaine office accepts a Logan County deed?
sections.html:
The Logan County recorder sits in the annex at 100 S. Madriver Street, Bellefontaine, OH 43311. The recorder's page gives 937-599-7201 as the phone number and lists the office as open Monday through Friday from 8:00 until 4:30. Wednesday is the day the office issues Veteran ID cards.

The office describes itself as keeper of the land ownership record and of every lien against land. It lists work under more than 1,000 Revised Code sections, stores records in archival form and indexes each filing so a searcher can trace ownership forward in time. Title examiners, attorneys, genealogists and historians all use those files.

The Logan Online portal lists a Recorder's Document Search for looking up filed documents. The recorder also publishes Document Standardization Guidelines, a historical page and a Veteran ID Card Program page.

sections.h2: What does the Logan County recorder charge?
sections.html:
A short schedule appears on the county's recordable documents page. Everything the recorder collects goes into the county general fund.

Logan County document filing fees
ItemFee
First 2 pages$39
Each additional page$8
Non-standardization fee$20
Marginal reference, each$4

Source: Logan County Recordable Documents.

Phone 937-599-7201 for a total on a lengthy document.

sections.h2: What layout rules can trigger the $20 fee in Logan County?
sections.html:
The extra $20 applies to paper that ignores Ohio Revised Code 317.114. Logan County's guidelines page ties the rule to documents prepared after June 30, 2009, and spells out the specifications:

  • Type no smaller than 10 point.
  • Sheets between letter size and legal size, meaning 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Ink in black or blue, with no highlighter marks.
  • One inch of white space along both sides and the foot of each page.
  • Three inches blank at the head of page one, held for stamps from the recorder, auditor and engineer.
  • An inch and a half blank at the head of every later page.

Five categories fall outside the rule: papers from a court or a taxing authority, plats, DD-214 discharge forms, state or federal documents, and anything signed before the law took effect. The page also offers a downloadable template.

sections.h2: What does the Logan County auditor do before the recorder?
sections.html:
A deed visits the county auditor first, and that office shares the 100 S. Madriver Street address. The auditor's forms page names the paperwork that can come into play:

  • Conveyance Form DTE 100 for an ordinary sale, and DTE 100M for a manufactured home.
  • Exempt Conveyance DTE 100EX, or 100MEX for a manufactured home.
  • Agriculture Conveyance DTE 102.
  • Homestead Conveyance DTE 101.
  • Owner Occupied Credit Application DTE 105C and the Homestead Exemption Application DTE 105A.
  • Destroyed Property Application DTE 26 for a building that no longer stands.

Logan County also posts a Survey and Conveyance Standards PDF for legal descriptions and an online Conveyance Fee Calculator. The state conveyance fee falls on the grantor under section 319.202, and a county transfer tax joins it only where commissioners adopted one under Chapter 322. The auditor can say which charges apply to your sale.

sections.h2: How does a Logan County forfeited land sale reach the recorder?
sections.html:
A parcel that went through tax foreclosure and drew no buyer in two offerings is forfeited to the State of Ohio and remanded to the auditor. The auditor's published auction rules describe a sale at the Logan County Courthouse Annex, 100 S. Madriver Street. Properties sell "As-Is" and "Buyer Beware," and the auditor gives no representation about possession, eviction or prior inspection.

The high bidder gets an Auditor's Deed. According to the rules, the auditor files it with the recorder and delivers it to the purchaser, and ownership passes at the moment the deed is delivered to the recorder. That deed extinguishes earlier title except for taxes and assessments not yet due, federal tax liens, easements and covenants running with the land. The rules bar a delinquent taxpayer or a current owner of the parcel from buying.

Bidders pay everything or leave at least $1,000 per parcel on sale day, and the remainder is due within 10 calendar days. The 2021 version of the rules also adds a 50 cent per parcel transfer charge and a 50 cent per parcel charge for envelope and postage, on top of recording.

sections.h2: When do Logan County property taxes come due, and how often is value reset?
sections.html:
The treasurer's site gave July 22, 2026 as the second-half due date and counted 38,426 parcels. The office sits at 100 S. Madriver Street, Suite D, and answers at (937) 599-7223 on weekdays between 8:00 AM and 4:30 PM. A county FAQ also describes an automatic withdrawal option that pulls the bill from a bank account on the last due date.

The auditor's FAQ lays out the cycle: a reappraisal each six years and a possible adjustment in the third calendar year after it. Taxable value is 35 percent of appraised value. The Ohio Department of Taxation's schedule puts Logan County in a 2028 update and a 2031 reappraisal. Formal complaints go to the Board of Revision, which accepts them from January 1 through March 31. Three officeholders sit on the board, the auditor, the treasurer and the president of the commissioners, or their representatives, and an owner can bring appraisals or comparable sales to the hearing.

sections.h2: What do county history and Census data say about Logan County?
sections.html:
Logan County lies in west central Ohio. The recorder's history page says it was cut from northern Champaign County in 1818 and named for Benjamin Logan. Hardin County was carved out of its northern portion in 1820 and began running its own affairs in 1833. Bellefontaine is the seat and only city, and Wikipedia places Campbell Hill, Ohio's highest natural point at 1,549 feet, northeast of the city.

Survey figures for 2020 to 2024 appear in the Census Bureau QuickFacts table:

  • Population reached 46,302 in July 2025, a 0.3 percent change from April 2020.
  • Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $203,200, and 77.6 percent of housing is owner-occupied.
  • Monthly owner costs: $1,326 with a loan, $601 without.
  • Rent at the median: $845 gross.
  • The 19,560 households report a median income of $71,551.
  • 24,071 housing units stood in the county in July 2025, and 120 permits were issued in 2025.

sections.h2: What is the recorder's role in Ohio, and what is Torrens land?
sections.html:
The recorder's history reaches back to the Northwest Territory of 1787, which gave every county such an office. Statehood in 1803 brought a rule that common pleas judges name the recorder. Voters took over the choice in 1829, and a four-year term has applied since 1936.

The recorder's page also covers Torrens registration. Where land is registered under the Torrens Act, its boundaries are certified and a state insurance fund backs the title, and the recorder handles those registered land records. A seller who owns an unusual rural tract should ask the Logan recorder whether any part of it was registered.

The auditor, the treasurer and the recorder all list 100 S. Madriver Street in Bellefontaine as their address, so a closing agent can take the transfer, the tax question and the recording to one building.

faqs.q: What is the filing fee for a short Logan County deed?
faqs.a: The posted schedule charges $39 for the opening two pages, then $8 for every page after that. A document that misses the layout standards picks up $20 more.

faqs.q: When can I visit the Logan County recorder?
faqs.a: The office at 100 S. Madriver Street in Bellefontaine opens weekdays at 8:00 and closes at 4:30. Its phone number is 937-599-7201.

faqs.q: Which papers skip the Logan County layout fee?
faqs.a: Court and taxing authority papers, plats, DD-214 discharge forms and state or federal documents are exempt, along with anything executed before the law began.

faqs.q: Does the Logan County recorder help fill out deed forms?
faqs.a: The office keeps and indexes records. Have a title company or attorney draft the deed, and phone 937-599-7201 with filing questions.

faqs.q: When does a forfeited land buyer own the property in Logan County?
faqs.a: Ownership passes when the auditor hands the Auditor's Deed to the recorder, according to the published auction rules. The auditor then sends the recorded deed to the purchaser.
